clue.text: Proportional representation given in three figures?

definitions.text: Proportional representation given in three figures?

parts.note: surface reading: the electoral system in which seats match share of the vote
setter's reading: a description of a person's body proportions, quoted as bust, waist and hip measurements

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like politics, with seats counted in three-figure numbers; read literally it means how a body's proportions are represented, as in 36-24-36.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial name for a woman's bust, waist and hip measurements, quoted as three numbers.

clue.text: City-dweller to live right next to ship

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
R is the standard abbreviation for right
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone wanting to live in a city settles down beside a ship in the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native or resident of Germany's capital, so the word names an inhabitant of one particular city.

clue.text: Sound of French pop duo

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so we want something pronounced like the French term

parts.note: pop is father, which in French is père

explanation.surface: A French pop act made up of two singers, and how they sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like music but means dad; the French for father, père, is said just like PAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two people or things together, exactly what a duo consists of.

clue.text: An emu three daughters trained for rider

indicators.note: something trained has been reshaped and drilled into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter, taken three times

explanation.surface: Three girls train an emu so that someone can ride it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a jockey, but it is the legal sense: a clause added to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an extra clause attached to a bill or contract, which is an item appended to a text.

clue.text: Deposit balance in Post Office without delay

indicators.note: one item sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: PO is the standard abbreviation for Post Office
the rest is the remainder or balance; deposit is part of the surface, as the balance left to put in

explanation.surface: Paying the outstanding amount into an account at the post office, and doing it promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like an instruction about money, but it just tells us to put one piece inside the other; the answer is a musical term for very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is used as an exclamation by conjurors for something happening instantly, so it means immediately or at once.

clue.text: Pack animal has problem with tendon

parts.note: a gang is a pack or group of people
a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: A beast of burden that is pulling up lame with a strained tendon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack animal' reads as one phrase, a mule or donkey, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a harmless cyst forming on a tendon sheath, usually at the wrist, so it is a medical complaint there.

clue.text: Rodent in the open an American soldier traps

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A

indicators.note: something that traps another holds it caught inside itself

parts.note: GI is the term for a US soldier
out means outside, in the open air

explanation.surface: A US soldier out in the field catches a small rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a long-legged burrowing rodent of Central and South America, related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Kind group almost always billets old dog

indicators.note: to billet is to house soldiers in a home, so the outer word lodges another inside it
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the preceding word is dropped

parts.note: a genre is a kind or type
a trio is a group of three
ever means always, as in ever after
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kindly group nearly always gives lodgings to some elderly dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective about the group, but it is a noun meaning sort; the lodger goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden retriever is a popular breed of gun dog with a gold coat, bred to fetch shot game.

clue.text: Just one left with Cinderella, beaten in National

indicators.note: something beaten has been battered out of its original shape, so the letters are rearranged
only a single left remaining means one of the doubled letters standing for left is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pantomime Cinderella left all alone, perhaps after losing at the National Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one of the two Ls from Cinderella, then rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, and an Icelander is a citizen of Iceland.

clue.text: Violence in the past involving King George

indicators.note: to involve is to include or take in, so one part wraps round the other

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in long ago
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as seen on postboxes

explanation.surface: Historical unrest in the reign of King George.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation or aggression, meaning trouble, fighting or hostile behaviour.

clue.text: Big feline seen first, not caught, free and threatening

indicators.note: not caught means without the letter for caught, as in cricket scoring, so it is removed
seen first places the second word ahead of the first one in the build

parts.note: a cat is a feline
large means big

explanation.surface: A big cat has escaped and is roaming loose and dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: C stands for caught on cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal or wild animal at large has escaped capture and is roaming free, posing a danger to the public.

clue.text: Hero in MiG crashing into sun died

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a crashing plane is wrecked and broken up, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A pilot hero dies as his MiG fighter plunges towards the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund is the warrior hero of the Norse Volsung saga, father of Sigurd, a legendary figure of great deeds.

clue.text: Writer George dresses knight in blue

indicators.note: to dress someone is to put clothes around them, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: blue means sad or down
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A writer named George puts a knight into blue clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin, author of Indiana and lover of Chopin.

clue.text: Warning poster having proposal about Ulster?

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, can be a poster

indicators.note: about means around, so one part is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting
Ulster is often used for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A political poster carrying a warning about a proposal for Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is strictly a nine-county province, but crosswords use it freely for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An admonition is a firm caution or reprimand, a stern piece of advice not to do something again.

clue.text: Patriarch sees a female supporter with Noah's son

parts.note: taken as written
a bra is a supporting undergarment worn by women
Ham was one of Noah's three sons, with Shem and Japheth

explanation.surface: A biblical patriarch meets a woman who backs Noah's son.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham is the founding father of the Israelites in Genesis, one of the three biblical patriarchs with Isaac and Jacob.

clue.text: Ambassador fashioned links with one city

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped or made anew, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diplomat builds ties with a single foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital and largest urban centre of Finland, on the Gulf of Finland.

clue.text: Goat god longing to show spirit

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god with a goat's legs and horns
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: The goat-legged god yearns to display his vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache means flamboyant confidence and verve, a dashing style that is a kind of high spirit.

clue.text: Bent author to keep repeating

parts.note: to pen is to write or author
to chant is to say the same words over and over

explanation.surface: A crooked writer who can't stop saying the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as dishonest or crooked, but it is a noun meaning a natural leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or inclination, which is what a bent for something is.

clue.text: Delivery service fellow provides

parts.note: a dinner service is a set of china
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A courier company man brings the parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests the post; in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and this term names a left-arm wrist-spinner's ball turning into a right-hander.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the term names a kind of ball bowled: a left-arm unorthodox spinner's delivery that turns from off to leg.

clue.text: Newspaper article by Belgian writer

parts.note: the i is a British national newspaper
an is the indefinite article
a Fleming is a Flemish-speaking Belgian

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by a writer from Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming was the British novelist who created James Bond, so he is a well-known author.

clue.text: Scots hooligan embracing trouble is done

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, putting arms around, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young lout or hooligan
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A Glasgow yob caught up in a spot of bother is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Done and nailed both mean caught or convicted, as when a crook is done or nailed for an offence.

clue.text: Complaint from youth in Spring month

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A youngster grumbling about something in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment, which is what a malady is.

clue.text: German booze stand at wake

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the German word for beer
second meaning: the frame a coffin rests on during mourning

explanation.surface: Germans drinking beer at a funeral gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: A wake is a vigil or gathering with the dead before burial, where drink often flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is German for beer, and in English it is the movable platform on which a corpse or coffin is laid.

clue.text: Six in court case that's unimportant

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court
VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: A minor court hearing involving six people.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little value or significance, petty and not worth worrying about.

clue.text: Security men only breaking tool

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one part splits the other

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool
a stag party or night is for men only

explanation.surface: Male security guards smash a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security' looks like guards, but it is a pledge held to guarantee a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held as a pledge that terms will be met, so they serve as security or collateral.

clue.text: Grain used in pudding — try it first

indicators.note: first tells us the second-named word comes at the front of the build

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: An invitation to sample some milk pudding before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal is an old convention, from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is the starchy granules from palm pith, cooked with milk to make a classic British nursery pudding.

clue.text: Arrest to put king in trouble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to halt or stop progress
second meaning: in chess, to threaten the opposing king

explanation.surface: A rebel plan to seize the monarch and land him in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to halt or restrain something, and in chess it means attacking the king directly.

clue.text: Blacken as one occupying room with fireplace

indicators.note: to occupy is to take up space within something, so this sits inside the other parts

parts.note: a den is a small private room
a grate is the metal frame of a fireplace
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sitting by the hearth in their den, smearing soot about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blacken' suggests soot from the fire, but here it means to defame someone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacken someone's name is to disparage or defame them, belittling their character unfairly.
